parties.petitioner: State of Andhra Pradesh (now State of Telangana)

summary: The appeals challenge the Errata Notification dated 13.3.2006 issued by the A.P. State Wakf Board, which added service Inam lands to a notified Wakf property. The State, infrastructure corporation, and land transferees contested the notification, arguing that it affected land already alienated for development projects. The High Court had dismissed writ petitions challenging the notification. Key issues included the validity of the Wakf Board's notification post-alienation, the status of land administration post-merger of Hyderabad State, and the applicability of statutory protections under land reform laws. The Court examined the historical administrative transitions in Hyderabad State, including the Military Governor's authority and subsequent regulations abolishing jagirs, upheld under constitutional provisions. The matter involved interpretation of Wakf law, property rights, and state alienation powers.
legal_provisions_cited: Article 31(6) of the Constitution of India
Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Jagirs (Commutation) Regulation, 1359 Fasli
Sarwanlal v. State of Hyderabad (Now Andhra Pradesh) & Ors. (AIR 1960 SC 862)
final_judgment: The appeals were disposed of, with the Court affirming the High Court's decision to dismiss the writ petitions and upholding the Errata Notification, subject to certain conditions ensuring that lawful alienations prior to the notification would not be disturbed.
